record.original_question: For unbounded linear operators A(t) on a Banach space X and for a starting time t0 , characterize the well-posedness of the non-autonomous Cauchy problem ẋ(t) = A(t)x(t) for t ≥ t0 x(t0 ) = x0 by Hille-Yosida type condition for an operator G generating an evolution semigroup on X = C0 (R, X) or X = Lp (R, X).

For unbounded linear operators A(t) on a Banach space X and for a starting time t0 , characterize the well-posedness of the non-autonomous Cauchy problem ẋ(t) = A(t)x(t) for t ≥ t0 x(t0 ) = x0 by Hille-Yosida type condition for an operator G generating an evolution semigroup on X = C0 (R, X) or X = Lp (R, X).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a Banach space and let $\{A(t)\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$ be a family of (in general unbounded) closed linear operators on $X$ with domains $D(A(t))\subseteq X$. For an initial time $t_0\in\mathbb{R}$ and initial datum $x_0\in X$, consider the non-autonomous abstract Cauchy problem
$$\dot{x}(t)=A(t)\,x(t),\quad t\geq t_0,\qquad x(t_0)=x_0.$$
The problem is said to be well-posed if there exists a strongly continuous evolution family $\{U(t,s)\}_{t\geq s}$ of bounded operators on $X$ (with $U(t,s)U(s,r)=U(t,r)$ and $U(s,s)=I$) such that, for sufficiently regular $x_0$, the function $t\mapsto U(t,t_0)x_0$ solves the problem.

On the function space $\mathcal{X}=C_0(\mathbb{R},X)$ or $\mathcal{X}=L^p(\mathbb{R},X)$ ($1\leq p<\infty$), the associated evolution semigroup $\{T(\tau)\}_{\tau\geq 0}$ is defined (formally) by
$$(T(\tau)f)(t)=U(t,t-\tau)\,f(t-\tau),$$
with infinitesimal generator $G$.

Problem. Find a Hille–Yosida-type characterization of the well-posedness of the non-autonomous Cauchy problem in terms of resolvent estimates on the generator $G$ of the evolution semigroup on $\mathcal{X}$. Specifically, provide necessary and sufficient conditions on $G$ (norm estimates on iterates of the resolvent $(\lambda - G)^{-1}$ analogous to the classical Hille–Yosida / Feller–Miyadera–Phillips conditions) ensuring that $G$ generates a strongly continuous evolution semigroup on $\mathcal{X}$ corresponding to a well-posed non-autonomous Cauchy problem governed by the family $\{A(t)\}$.
artifact.category_tag: evolution semigroups and non-autonomous Cauchy problems
artifact.status_search_result: The literature on evolution semigroups for non-autonomous Cauchy problems (Howland–Evans–Neidhardt–Nickel–Räbiger–Schnaubelt and others) develops sufficient conditions and partial characterizations, but a complete Hille–Yosida-type generation theorem giving necessary and sufficient resolvent conditions characterizing well-posedness of general non-autonomous Cauchy problems remains unavailable; standard references state that a uniform Hille–Yosida-style generation theorem for non-autonomous Cauchy problems is not known. The problem therefore appears to be open.

status_evidence.title: Well-Posedness and Asymptotic Behaviour of Non-Autonomous Linear Evolution Equations
status_evidence.snippet: Evolution semigroups associated to evolution families on C_0(R,X) and L^p(R,X) and their role in characterizing well-posedness.
status_evidence.claim: Evolution semigroup approach provides a framework but not a complete Hille-Yosida characterization.

status_evidence.title: Evolution semigroups for nonautonomous Cauchy problems
status_evidence.snippet: One-to-one correspondence between evolution families and evolution semigroups; sufficient conditions for generation are studied.
status_evidence.claim: Partial generation results exist; a full Hille–Yosida-type characterization is not established.
